nodes.label: BS_RenderSceneShadowContexts
nodes.rationale: Central scene dispatcher that constructs FShadowMaskSceneContext on the stack; confirmed live via RTTI, exact bytes, and Frida with 125 calls in a six-second sample.

nodes.label: FObjectShadowDepthPass11::UploadConstants
nodes.rationale: Owns the ObjectShadowDepth VS/PS constants; identified as the native shadow producer boundary rather than an inferred D3D lane.

nodes.label: FShadowDepthTestPass11::UploadConstants
nodes.rationale: Native shadow-test reconstruction/resource binder that owns screenToShadowBuffer (c17-c20) and scene depth; the true screen-space attenuation-mask producer.

nodes.label: FPlayerSceneNode::vftable
nodes.rationale: Transient player scene node whose live heap address must never be persisted; only guarded RVA/signature hooks are safe.

nodes.label: AShockPlayer::vftable
nodes.rationale: Exact identity filter for the roomscale movement probe; owns first-person AHands at +0x724.

nodes.label: AHands::vftable
nodes.rationale: Exact first-person hands actor; mesh +0x128, skeleton +0x3fc, animation adapter +0x408, AimIK wrapper +0x40c.

nodes.label: AimIKTargetTracker Constructor
nodes.rationale: Engine-owned 0x180-byte native tracker; must never be allocated manually, only created through the natural capability-bit recreation seam.

nodes.label: D3D11Hooks module
nodes.rationale: Grew to roughly 18,000 lines while proving unknown render/engine routes; the refactor must preserve validated runtime behavior, not redesign stereo math while moving code.

nodes.label: D3D11Hooks.cpp god-file extraction decision
nodes.rationale: Keep hook callbacks thin, prefer explicit state objects over new mutable externs, and build/runtime-test at stable checkpoints so ownership refactors stay separated from renderer experiments in Git history.

nodes.label: bioshockvr_injector --compatibility-report
nodes.rationale: Line-oriented static host report (Windows build, DXGI adapters, OpenXR runtime manifest) is not itself a compatibility claim; it must be paired with a complete live session log.

nodes.label: Evidence label taxonomy (Confirmed live / Static confirmed / Hypothesis / Dead end)
0.3.191-internald3dguard build
nodes.rationale: Live-confirmed crash containment: internal-D3D guard active, one pacing-only READY frame, SYNCHRONIZED->VISIBLE->FOCUSED transition, and at least 1,440 focused frames with zero Present failures.

nodes.label: 0.3.192-layerrestore build
nodes.rationale: Deliberately re-enabled the Motion Compensation implicit layer on top of the 0.3.191 containment stack; reached frame 35 then reproduced the identical Virtual Desktop fail-fast, rejecting the layer.

nodes.label: 0.3.193-motioncompguard build
nodes.rationale: Restores process-local Motion Compensation isolation as active/packaged/no-INI default while preserving every 0.3.191 containment fix; current handoff build awaiting a clean containment run.

nodes.label: InternalD3DCallGuard (thread-local guard)
nodes.rationale: Prevents BioShockVR's own OpenXR fullscreen blit, source copies, and runtime-owned D3D/DXGI calls from recursively re-entering game draw classification, HUD capture, and shadow probes.

nodes.label: OpenXR startup state-aware visibility handshake
nodes.rationale: Repolls OpenXR events immediately after xrWaitFrame and touches no eye image until session state is VISIBLE/FOCUSED, closing a race where a long blocking wait left stale READY state driving rendering.

nodes.label: Virtual Desktop LibOVRRT32_1 fail-fast crash (0xC0000409 reason 7)
nodes.rationale: Repeating crash at VirtualDesktop.LibOVRRT32_1.dll+0x1e98c wrapping a freed-object execute access violation (0xDEDEDEDE) during D3D11/OpenXR texture-swapchain cleanup; begins only after BioShockVR injection.

nodes.label: 0.3.187-shadowownership redesign
nodes.rationale: Regenerates the screen-space attenuation mask per eye at full private-eye dimensions using a frozen per-eye depth SRV and isolated copied depth/stencil surface, instead of using the live private world DSV as shadow scratch space.

nodes.label: Projected-light/gobo screen-space defect
nodes.rationale: The largest unresolved visual problem: a mono/center-camera screen-space shadow/light mask sampled by per-eye geometry produces a stretched gobo and a stale neutral desktop-wrench silhouette.

nodes.label: Snap-turn body/gameplay yaw ownership problem
nodes.rationale: Head-pose yaw bias and native mouse-yaw impulses both changed only the rendered view, not BioShock's movement/weapon/body heading; a correct snap turn must mutate the same AShockPlayerController yaw owner used by gameplay.

nodes.label: engine_object_census (0.3.178 read-only RE build)
nodes.rationale: Bounded telemetry confirming the exact AShockPlayer -> AHands -> mesh/skeleton/animation/AimIK chain and AWrench vtable slot 76 target, reducing dependence on manual Cheat Engine/x32dbg scans.

nodes.label: Native AimIK creation lifecycle problem
nodes.rationale: AHands +0x40c (the AimIK wrapper) stays null in attach-to-running sessions because the engine-owned AimIKTargetTracker is only created during a natural AHands animation-member recreation; suspended-launch injection is required to test it.

nodes.label: Downstream foreground basis-ownership experiment (0.3.176)
nodes.rationale: Captures the authored wrench/arm mount once and reconstructs orientation from the live controller-relative-to-head basis instead of appending a controller delta to an already camera-contaminated model-view matrix.

nodes.label: VR-primary desktop-foreground suppression (0.3.184)
nodes.rationale: Skips the original desktop foreground draw once a foreground row successfully replays into private eyes; suppression fired heavily but did not visibly improve the projected-light defect, weakening it as the direct cause.

nodes.label: Authored idle-pose time/rate freeze (0.3.166)
nodes.rationale: Holds one authored idle animation frame through native SkeletonInstance position/rate setters while preserving weight, after zero-weight suppression was falsified as a usable resting policy.

nodes.label: Shared wrench-root rigid-group pivot (0.3.162)
nodes.rationale: Uses the wrench root as a shared post-animation rigid pivot for both the 576-byte wrench and 832-byte hand/forearm rows since the hand draw is CPU/pre-skinned with no GPU bone palette.

nodes.label: Reusable per-eye matrix cbuffer cache
nodes.rationale: Reuses per-context/per-eye dynamic constant buffers via WRITE_DISCARD instead of creating two D3D11 buffers per applied draw, removing a large recoverable CPU/driver cost.

nodes.label: Late-LDR HUD tee and head-locked OpenXR quad
nodes.rationale: Tees the confirmed final-LDR UI shader pair into a transparent private target rather than compositing the full desktop backbuffer, avoiding duplicated world geometry and tonemapping.

nodes.label: HMD-forward binocular reference reticle (0.3.143)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not the gameplay crosshair; placed independently per eye at a configured convergence plane because the private-HDR headset source precedes BioShock's late-LDR desktop crosshair.

nodes.label: Physical wrench-swing velocity classifier (0.3.169)
nodes.rationale: Telemetry-only hysteretic OR-threshold over dominant-grip velocity; explicitly performs no attack, collision, or damage call pending correlation with BioShock's authored collision-active window.

nodes.label: BS4_wrench.rdc capture
nodes.rationale: Equipped-wrench RenderDoc capture exposing exact HDR foreground signatures (11088-index wrench at 576 bytes, 26178-index hand/forearm at 832 bytes) used across nearly every viewmodel/lighting/shadow probe.

nodes.label: RenderDoc 32-bit address-space exhaustion crash
nodes.rationale: Equipped-wrench RenderDoc captures crash BioShockHD.exe inside renderdoc.dll's intentional fatal allocation path because the paused 32-bit process has no contiguous free region large enough for the scratch allocation.

nodes.label: Do not re-enable the 32-bit Motion Compensation implicit layer
Do not feed OpenXR/runtime D3D work back through game-render hooks
Do not use session state sampled before a blocking xrWaitFrame
Do not implement comfort blackout by dropping to zero OpenXR layers
Do not treat head-pose yaw bias as a complete snap turn
Do not implement snap turn as a long synthetic right-stick pulse
Do not classify loose pickup props as equipped foreground from index count alone
Do not re-enable the old live-DSV per-eye shadow-mask producer
nodes.rationale: Two consecutive Virtual Desktop dumps (40412, 68008) fail-fast during D3D11/OpenXR texture-swapchain cleanup while the live-DSV shadow-mask route was enabled.

nodes.label: Do not solve foreground HMD bleed with another additive camera-relative delta
Do not combine attach-mode null AimIK with absolute grip ownership
Do not interpret a null cached shader as a null live shader after late injection
Do not infer the shadow-test contract from the first 16 vec4 rows
Do not diagnose the neutral hand/wrench cutout from final eye color alone
Do not stop all first-person animations or remove idle weight
Do not manually allocate AimIK or force hand animation recreation
Do not broaden viewmodel lighting correction by cbuffer size alone
Do not move weapon origins or double-apply head aim
Do not turn a velocity threshold into direct wrench damage
Never flap synthetic controller presence after explicit VR activation
Recenter yaw/height without leveling pitch or roll
A shadow consumer is not sufficient evidence for guessed pass replay
Do not infer compatibility from hardware inventory alone
Do not treat LOCAL as a persistent floor origin
Do not package dirty builds or let uninstall own user data implicitly
Do not hook shader registration functions as camera writers
nodes.rationale: Xrefs to strings like worldViewProj lead only to shader parameter registration functions (e.g. FUN_11079000), not runtime camera/projection writers.

nodes.label: Do not trust current MCP cbuffer numeric values
nodes.rationale: get_cbuffer_contents returns valid names/layouts but all-zero numeric values for tested draws; raw buffer bytes must be verified another way.

nodes.label: Never expand BioShock's bounded source scissor during private replay
nodes.rationale: Replacing a bounded 1920x279 source scissor with a full-target scissor turned a bounded vista/capture pass into the cyan/exterior-city shell and sharply increased frame cost.

nodes.label: PS-null SRV bindings are not shadow-consumer proof
nodes.rationale: D3D11 retains stage bindings across draws, so a depth/stencil-only draw can carry a stale PS SRV without ever sampling it; consumer classification must require a live pixel shader.

nodes.label: AShockHUD::RenderHealthBars is not the fixed player meter path
Screen-space SRV fallback range is diagnostic, not a universal fix
nodes.rationale: Broadening the target-sized screen-space SRV fallback (e.g. indexed-primitive family-wide) regressed boulders, poster frames, and rubble even though it helped one artifact class.

nodes.label: Git safety-rail and .gitignore policy
nodes.rationale: Ghidra/RenderDoc databases, captures, dumps, logs, crash dumps, and extracted game assets are intentionally excluded from Git so BioShockVR history stays reviewable and free of proprietary/generated material.

nodes.label: Torso-space AimIK target model (not direct HMD ownership)
nodes.rationale: Native player/controller yaw should own planar torso heading and HMD position should translate the shoulder centre, while HMD pitch/roll and head-only yaw must not rotate the shoulder bar.

nodes.label: Center-depth attenuation-mask hypothesis for the shadow/gobo defect
nodes.rationale: The stretched shadow is BioShock's ShadowDepthTestPS reconstructing center-camera scene depth into the shadow buffer and writing a multiplicative screen-space mask, not a conventional per-eye shadow.

nodes.label: Snap turn must change BioShock body heading, not the rendered head residual
nodes.rationale: Ghidra confirms the mouse-yaw impulse only reaches UGamepadPlayerInput::CalculateInput and the PlayerInput dispatcher, not the controller rotator, so it never establishes real yaw ownership.

nodes.label: P_center extraction from screenDataToCamera
nodes.rationale: BioShock's real center projection matrix is decoded from raw VS $Globals bytes (RenderDoc cbuffer helper returns all zeros): fixed 100-degree horizontal FOV, aspect-derived vertical FOV, near~10/far~65536 game units.

nodes.label: Direct same-frame draw replay can bridge cloned-buffer proof to real stereo
nodes.rationale: Live-confirmed clean world-route draws can be replayed twice with forced left/right cloned constants into the same HDR target, but this only proves plumbing, not per-eye render-target routing.

nodes.label: Temporal OpenXR eye cache must use fresh stereo candidates
nodes.rationale: The temporal bridge must clear stale cached eye textures and fall back to the live mono frame instead of repeatedly submitting the last ready stereo pair after proof work stops.

nodes.label: Private per-eye HDR/depth targets bridge same-target proof to true stereo
nodes.rationale: Confirmed progression: scout allocation, bind/draw/restore, private-present accumulation, and the XR fullscreen eye-blit sampling copied private HDR eye targets in the headset.

nodes.label: OpenXR-sized private eye targets replace 16:9 crop presentation
nodes.rationale: Allocating private HDR/depth eye targets at the OpenXR eye extent and using runtime per-eye FOV projection removes the zoom caused by cropping a 16:9 source into a tall eye texture.

nodes.label: Live shadow producer uses compact 320-byte VS state
nodes.rationale: The 0.3.159 per-eye shadow producer attempted 191,950 times but applied zero because every bounded producer row used vs0=320 instead of the RenderDoc-derived 400-byte assumption.

nodes.label: UEVR prior-art architecture lessons
nodes.rationale: UEVR is not directly portable but supports splitting BioShockVR into explicit XR runtime, D3D render bridge, stereo replay, engine camera, input, UI, and diagnostic lanes.

nodes.label: Vengeance engine (UE2.5 fork) static findings
nodes.rationale: Non-stock package serialization, external .blk/Catalog.bdc bulk resources, ShaderTag-to-MaterialFactory routing, and BSP lightmap/luminance UV construction distinguish BioShock's engine from stock Unreal tooling.

nodes.label: Wrench pickup object and equipped viewmodel use distinct HDR sublanes
nodes.rationale: Pre-pickup floor wrench uses a 512-byte world $Globals layout, while the equipped wrench/hand uses separate 544/576-byte and 752/832-byte HDR foreground sublanes, not final LDR UI.

nodes.label: Install-Or-Update-BioShockVR.ps1
nodes.rationale: Installs managed program files under %LOCALAPPDATA%\BioShockVR, creates the user INI from packaged motion-control defaults on first install, and preserves an existing user INI across updates.

nodes.label: Set-BioShockVRCalibration.ps1
nodes.rationale: Backs up the active INI before changing only its three owned stance/reference-space/eye-height keys; LOCAL space always ignores a stored eye height because it is session-relative.

nodes.label: High-level BioShockVR rendering pipeline flow
nodes.rationale: BioShock world draws pass through D3D11 hooks, route/cbuffer classification, an eligible private left/right HDR+depth replay, per-eye WVP mutation, and an OpenXR fullscreen eye blit/tonemap before projection submission.

nodes.label: BioShockVR Project Phases tracker (B0-B7, 88 tasks)
nodes.rationale: Shared Google Sheet roadmap weighted YES=100%/BUILT=75%/EXPLORING=35%/NO or BLOCKED=0%; last synced 2026-07-21 at YES=11, BUILT=40, EXPLORING=11, NO=26, 51.0% weighted completion.

hyperedges.note: The internal-D3D guard and the visibility handshake first appeared together and were never independently A/B tested; together they are confirmed live to survive at least 1,440 focused frames without the Virtual Desktop fail-fast.

hyperedges.label: Native BioShock shadow-mask render chain
hyperedges.note: Exact static/live byte matches plus a bounded Frida trace confirmed this dispatcher chain on the render thread, identifying ShadowDepthTestPS as the true screen-space attenuation-mask owner including screenToShadowBuffer c17-c20.

hyperedges.label: Native AimIK lifecycle proof chain
hyperedges.note: The engine-owned tracker, the AHands +0x40c wrapper slot, the confirmed-null attach-to-running lifecycle finding, and the torso-space target-model design all describe one unresolved proof chain: suspended-launch injection must create the wrapper before joint/target mutation is trusted.
